issue: Under § 404 of the First Step Act, may a district court resentencing a covered offense consider intervening changes in case law, not just the Fair Sentencing Act's changes, when recalculating the sentence?
provision: First Step Act of 2018, § 404 (Fair Sentencing Act §§ 2 and 3)

sides.position: No. The court must place itself in the counterfactual world where only Fair Sentencing Act §§ 2 and 3 applied and must not consider other legal changes, including intervening case law. The First Step Act does not authorize a plenary resentencing.
cases: United States v. Kelley, 962 F.3d 470 (9th Cir. 2020)
United States v. Hegwood, 934 F.3d 414 (5th Cir. 2019)
United States v. Smith, 958 F.3d 494 (6th Cir. 2020)

sides.position: Yes. A court may consider at least some intervening changes in case law when recalculating a prisoner's sentence under the First Step Act, because the statute contains no limiting language barring it.
cases: United States v. Chambers, 956 F.3d 667 (4th Cir. 2020)

this_court: No. The Ninth Circuit holds that a district court may consider only the Fair Sentencing Act changes in its counterfactual inquiry, and it rejects Chambers.
quote: In reaching this conclusion, we deepen a circuit split.
cite: United States v. Ezralee Kelley, 962 F.3d 470 (9th Cir. 2020)
